recentItems.title: Lil Durk on Helping His Jailed Crew: We Got 20 Guys Locked Up (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, Lil Durk opened up about the “fake friends” he realized he had after being arrested and denied bail on a gun possession charge. After his release, Durk took to Twitter to call out those who didn’t show him support while he was locked up.

In this exclusive clip, the “Dis Ain’t What U Want” rapper discussed the support he provides to his incarcerated “brothers” and how he didn’t receive nearly the same level of support during his own time behind bars. Durk explained that he makes sure his incarcerated friends have anything they need while serving their time, revealing that “like, 20 of the guys” were locked up.

Brian “Glaze” Gibbs sits down with Vlad to break down the long-running Jam Master Jay murder case and why the Run-DMC legend’s 2002 killing still raises questions in hip-hop history. Gibbs says he knew Ronald Washington from Rikers Island in 1981, while Vlad reviews the complicated federal case involving Washington, Carl Jordan Jr., and Jay Bright, including convictions, an overturned murder conviction, a guilty plea, DNA evidence, and sentencing issues.  

The conversation also explores allegations that the murder was tied to a drug deal, references Southwest T, and examines how fame, financial pressure, loyalty, and dangerous circles can collide in the music industry. Gibbs reflects on Jam Master Jay’s legacy, his influence on rap culture, and the tragedy of being harmed by people close to him.

--------
Former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill joins VladTV to break down life aboard U.S. Navy ships amid reports of the USS Abraham Lincoln spending roughly 250 days at sea. Drawing on his own deployments, including time on the USS Austin and visits to Bahrain, O’Neill explains carrier conditions, food supplies, sailor morale, retention, and the realities of long military cruises. The conversation then turns to global flashpoints, including Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Manama’s U.S. naval presence, and President Donald Trump’s comments about American control in the region. O’Neill also offers his view on Greenland and why he believes future U.S. strategy could involve bold territorial moves. Vlad and O’Neill close with a candid exchange about military service, geopolitics, and what the Navy is built to handle.

--------
Hit-Boy breaks down the music-industry battle behind his long-running producer deal, explaining how Roc Nation, Jay-Z and Desiree Perez stepped in while he was managed by the company. In conversation with Elliott Wilson and Vlad, the Grammy-winning producer says years of emails and frustration with Universal Music Group led to talks involving top executives, including Jody Gerson, but that a full release in 2021 was denied. Instead, he says he was given a 2025 end date after being tied to the contract since 2007.

The discussion expands into the harsh math of record labels, artist development and why successful producers often subsidize failed signings. Hit-Boy also reflects on Dr. Dre’s track record, staying motivated when records don’t immediately hit No. 1, investing in his father’s music, and measuring success through growth as a rapper and artist. A candid look at contracts, ownership, Roc Nation, UMG and hip-hop business realities.

recentItems.title: Mafia Prosecutor Ed McDonald Tells The Real "Goodfellas" Story (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:
Watch the FULL uncensored interview early - become a VladTV YouTube Member now:
https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Former federal prosecutor Ed McDonald sits down with VladTV to discuss his legendary career fighting organized crime and the real-life Mafia figures and investigations that helped inspire the classic film Goodfellas.

McDonald traces his career from clerking for federal judge Anthony Travia to joining the Manhattan DA’s office and eventually the Brooklyn Organized Crime Strike Force in 1977. He explains how federal prosecutors coordinated with the FBI, NYPD, and IRS to investigate some of New York’s most powerful Mafia families.

A major portion of the interview focuses on the 1978 Lufthansa robbery at JFK Airport. As coordinating prosecutor, McDonald investigated the multimillion-dollar heist and explains how mob associate Henry Hill eventually became a government informant, providing information that connected Jimmy Burke and others to organized crime. Hill’s cooperation also exposed the Boston College point-shaving scandal, leading investigators into another major prosecution involving Burke and college basketball players.

McDonald also discusses cases involving the Bonanno and Gambino crime families, including prosecuting Joseph Massino before later becoming his defense attorney when Massino decided to cooperate with the government. He recalls overseeing legal work surrounding electronic surveillance of Gambino boss Paul Castellano, whose conversations provided investigators with critical evidence before his assassination by John Gotti’s crew.

The conversation also explores McDonald’s unexpected connection to Hollywood. After meeting director Martin Scorsese, McDonald was cast as himself in Goodfellas, appearing in the famous scene where Henry and Karen Hill enter the Witness Protection Program.

McDonald concludes by reflecting on controversial cooperation deals, admitting that prosecutors may have been too lenient with certain informants. He also discusses threats against prosecutors, the dangers of confronting the Mafia, and the assassination of prosecutor William Aronwald.

--------
DJ Vlad sits down with former Brooklyn street figure Brian “Glaze” Gibbs for a candid conversation about change, ego, violence, and the cost of freedom. Asked what he would do if Vlad slapped him, Gibbs reflects on his first instincts versus the reality of losing everything he has rebuilt after prison. He contrasts his mindset with Terrance “Gangsta” Williams, discussing regret, restraint, “snitching,” loyalty, and the pressure people face when confronted with life sentences.

The interview also turns to the Pappy Mason case, the killing of a rookie police officer and a parole officer, and Gibbs’ claims about being arrested as a suspect while others were released. Gibbs speaks on Pat, Cat, Scott’s release, prison consequences, family, and why real change matters after decades in the streets and the penitentiary. A raw VladTV discussion on accountability, redemption, and survival.

Hit-Boy, Elliott Wilson and Vlad revisit one of hip-hop’s most debated legal stories: Duane “Keefe D” Davis’ statements about the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur and how his VladTV interviews may now factor into the Las Vegas trial. The conversation connects Hit-Boy’s *HITstory* reflections on the East Coast vs. West Coast era, Tupac, The Notorious B.I.G., Orlando Anderson, and the long-running rumors surrounding the case.

Vlad explains that Keefe D had already published a book and believed a proffer agreement protected him before discussing the events publicly. Elliott Wilson questions how those interviews helped bring Keefe D’s version of events into wider view, while Hit-Boy weighs in on justice, closure for Tupac’s family, and the impact of revisiting decades-old street history in court. The discussion also touches on media responsibility, incriminating interviews, and Vlad’s past decision involving Drakeo the Ruler.

--------
Former federal prosecutor Ed McDonald joins Vlad to revisit the March 20, 1987 Queens shooting tied to the Colombo crime family, when a mob-ordered attack meant for former Organized Crime Strike Force prosecutor William Aronwald instead killed his 78-year-old father, George Aronwald. McDonald discusses what was known at the time, later allegations involving Colombo boss Carmine Persico, and why the botched hit remains a grim example of organized crime retaliation.

The conversation also turns to McDonald’s new book, *Chasing Goodfellas*, covering the Lufthansa case, Henry Hill, point shaving, and his role in the making of Martin Scorsese and Nick Pileggi’s *Goodfellas*. McDonald previews future books on John Gotti, Paul Castellano, Joseph Massino, the Gambino, Bonanno, Colombo and Lucchese families, plus the Abscam investigation that convicted members of Congress and Senator Harrison Williams.

recentItems.description:

Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 12: https://youtu.be/114WBdepUVw
Part 1: https://youtu.be/fA-LpsSTDUs
--------
Former SEAL Team Six operator Robert O’Neill sits down with Vlad to break down the pay behind one of the most consequential missions in U.S. military history: the Abbottabad, Pakistan raid that killed Osama bin Laden. O’Neill says he was earning E-7 pay with combat-related incentives—about $80,000 a year—and explains why the team did not receive a bonus or the reported $50 million reward.

The conversation also covers CIA sources in Afghanistan, the risks faced by informants, and the rescue mission tied to Marcus Luttrell, the Navy SEAL whose story inspired *Lone Survivor*. O’Neill reflects on Pashtunwali, Taliban threats, and the tension between special operations teams and intelligence agencies.

He also discusses his next chapter with The Operators Collective, featuring former military leaders including Dakota Meyer, plus events in New York, Las Vegas, leadership training, combatives, and upcoming work around Ryan Garcia’s fight.
